newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Liberals back Martin on no broad tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Liberals back Martin on no broad tax cut.

text.p: Canada's Liberals on Friday backed Finance Minister Paul Martin's refusal for now to make broad-based tax cuts.

The working group on deficit reduction and tax policy at the biennial Liberal convention defeated a resolution from the Manitoba Liberals to reduce the national Goods and Services Tax rate "or utilize other means to provide relief."
Instead it passed a resolution to provide an income tax system "in which taxpayers share the tax burden fairly" and which promotes "greater cooperation among the various levels of government."
That resolution goes to Sunday morning's final plenary session of the convention.

The Conservative and Reform parties, anticipating a general election expected next year, have called for significant income tax relief. They and the separatist Bloc Quebecois have also called for lower unemployment insurance premiums.
Martin, who attended the Liberal policy workshop, repeated his policy of not bringing in a broad-based tax cut at this time.
